priorFamilyDisposition.reason: Repeated separate satellite pylon and thin bridge/slab grammar.

hypothesis: A single broad front-elevation cathedral silhouette extruded through real depth will make the inhabited lower palace the primary mass. Domes become deeply embedded roof bays rather than separate tower caps, and the keep grows out of the same hull.
requiredTopology: Create one closed, continuous extruded cathedral hull spanning at least 3.20 world units wide, at least 1.90 deep, and at least 1.75 tall above the palace plinth.
The hull's front elevation must carry a broad stepped shoulder silhouette and central upper rise; it must not be a flat rectangular facade slab.
The central keep must overlap the hull by at least 45 percent of its visible height and at least 70 percent of its footprint so it visibly emerges from the inhabited body.
Front shoulder domes must be embedded into broad body bays: no more than 45 percent of each dome may project above its bay collar and there may be no exposed drum taller than 0.45 world units.
Rear shoulder domes must remain mostly behind and fused into the deep hull; no ring of freestanding towers.
Preserve closed upper-hemisphere roof topology and the compact crown solution from family v6.
Keep the total structural width within 3.20 to 3.45 and total macro height within 3.60 to 3.90 relative to the 4.70 court diameter.
frontRead: Large central entrance volume and occupied lower floors dominate the lower half.
Four domed bays are subordinate shoulders nested into the cathedral.
Central hero dome and compact crown provide the vertical climax.
strictRejects: Any satellite with a visible pylon/drum taller than its dome diameter.
Any thin horizontal bridge or wedge serving as the only connection between tower and body.
Any visible empty court gap between palace body and a supposed shoulder bay.
A central thin keep standing on a low platform with separate towers around it.
A flat single-depth facade card, open-backed shell, or unclosed roof.

evidence.gate: All required view/category scores at least 0.85; worst view governs. One bounded correction maximum for this family.
